name: Industrial control misconfiguration
blurb: Claims where process control AI makes improper adjustments in plants or refineries.
summary: Claims where process control AI makes improper adjustments in plants or refineries.
parent_name: Model Liability and Errors and Omissions

part_3_high_value_red_flags: Absolute pollution exclusion that bars coverage for any release of hydrocarbons or chemicals even when caused by a sudden and accidental control system failure.
Professional services exclusion that removes coverage for the design, configuration or maintenance of the process control AI, leaving the plant owner without defense for the core error.
Cyber or electronic data exclusion that treats any software malfunction, including non malicious misconfiguration, as an excluded cyber event rather than a covered physical damage cause.
Care, custody or control exclusion that eliminates coverage for damage to the plant's own equipment while the AI is actively controlling that equipment.
Your product or your work exclusion that bars coverage for damage to the plant's output or to the control system installation performed by the insured contractor.
Impaired property or loss of use exclusion that denies third party business interruption claims when the only damage is the inability to use the plant's product or service.
Sublimit for electronic data or software errors that caps loss at a fraction of the probable maximum loss from a full plant shutdown.
manuscript_wording_and_carve_backs: Delete or narrow the professional services exclusion to affirmatively cover bodily injury and property damage arising from negligent configuration, testing or maintenance of process control AI.

Add an affirmative endorsement covering physical damage and business interruption caused by non malicious software errors, logic flaws or incorrect setpoints in industrial control systems, overriding any silent cyber exclusion.
Replace the absolute pollution exclusion with a sudden and accidental pollution buyback that responds to releases caused by control system failure, including gradual releases over a defined period.
Add a failure to perform carve back that covers third party property damage or bodily injury when the AI system fails to operate as specified, without requiring a separate product defect.
Add a contingent time element extension for dependent properties, including pipelines, storage terminals and customer facilities, that suffer loss due to the plant's shutdown.
Add a waiver of subrogation against the AI vendor and control system integrator, and name them as additional insureds on the plant owner's liability policy where required by contract.
Add a defense outside limits provision for AI related claims so that defense costs do not erode the indemnity limit, given the high cost of technical expert witnesses and root cause analysis.

part_4_program_structure_and_limits.bi_waiting_period: Business interruption waiting period typically 24 to 72 hours for process control failures but negotiable down to 12 hours for continuous process plants where any downtime immediately stops revenue.
part_4_program_structure_and_limits.business_interruption: Gross earnings and extra expense coverage for loss of production due to an AI misconfiguration, including contingent business interruption from loss of feedstock, utility supply or downstream customer demand caused by the same event, with an extended period of indemnity for restart, recalibration and regulatory inspection.
part_4_program_structure_and_limits.property_eb_equipment: Electronic data processing equipment and industrial control system hardware including distributed control systems, programmable logic controllers, sensors, actuators and safety instrumented systems covered on a replacement cost basis with agreed value for custom or obsolete AI hardware.
part_4_program_structure_and_limits.per_occurrence_primary_excess_layered_pr: Primary all risk property policy with a per occurrence limit set by the site's estimated maximum foreseeable loss from a runaway reaction, overpressure or fire following an AI misadjustment, layered with excess property policies attaching above the primary retention and any captive or self insured layer.

part_2_paper_type_and_limit_structure.cgl_primary: Primary commercial general liability with per occurrence and aggregate limits sized to the plant's maximum foreseeable loss from a single process upset, typically layered above a self insured retention that reflects the operator's risk appetite and loss history.
part_2_paper_type_and_limit_structure.paper_basis: Occurrence based for the plant operator's third party bodily injury and property damage because the harm manifests at the moment of the improper adjustment or the resulting physical event, while claims made applies to the AI developer's errors and omissions for financial loss that may be discovered long after the configuration error.
part_2_paper_type_and_limit_structure.excess_umbrella_towers: Excess liability towers in multiple layers with attachment points set by the primary limit and each layer following form to the primary except for negotiated drop down provisions when an underlying aggregate is exhausted by multiple AI related events.

part_1_core_third_party_liability_exposu: Bodily injury to plant workers or nearby residents from fire, explosion or toxic gas release triggered by an improper valve or heater adjustment.
Third party property damage to adjacent facilities, pipelines or transportation infrastructure from overpressure, runaway reaction or spill.
Environmental cleanup and natural resource damages from an uncontrolled release of hydrocarbons or chemicals caused by a misconfigured setpoint.
Business interruption losses of downstream customers or suppliers who depend on the plant's output and suffer loss of use after a shutdown.
Products liability if the plant's off spec product causes damage or injury after shipment due to a process deviation.
Professional liability of the AI developer or control system integrator for negligent configuration, inadequate testing or failure to warn of known instability.
Contractual liability assumed by the plant owner in supply or service agreements that allocate process safety risk to the operator.

underwriter_wants_to_know: What process variables the AI controls and the maximum deviation it can command before a hard wired safety interlock trips.
Whether the AI operates in open loop advisory mode or closed loop direct actuation of valves, pumps, compressors or heaters.
How often the AI model is retrained and what validation testing is performed against a digital twin of the plant before deployment.
What human override and manual shutdown procedures exist and the maximum time for an operator to intervene after an alert.
Whether the AI vendor or integrator carries separate professional liability and cyber insurance and the contractual indemnity from that vendor to the plant owner.
The age and redundancy of the underlying distributed control system and safety instrumented system that the AI interfaces with.
Any prior near misses, process upsets or regulatory citations linked to automated control changes.
